David Hockney
A collection of Hockney's iPad drawings capturing the changing view from his window, celebrated for their vibrant, digital-medium immediacy.

History Of The British Empire For The Use Of Schools In British North America / by William Francis Collier Paperback | Indigo Chapters.


Attributes
  • Mpn: 9781179710884

This book compiles a series of vibrant drawings David Hockney created on his iPad, each depicting the view from his window at different times of day and across changing seasons. The collection captures Hockney's ongoing fascination with light, color, and perception, while also highlighting his enthusiastic embrace of digital tools as a serious artistic medium late in his career.
The Beatles
Photographer Harry Benson's behind-the-scenes shots of The Beatles during their whirlwind touring years.

Photographer Harry Benson's behind-the-scenes shots of The Beatles during their whirlwind touring years.

Attributes
  • Mpn: B001970002
  • Weight: 0.2

Photojournalist Harry Benson had unprecedented access to The Beatles during the height of Beatlemania, capturing the band on tour, backstage, and in candid off-guard moments across the US and beyond. This collection offers an intimate, fly-on-the-wall look at the exhaustion, excitement, and camaraderie of the band during their most explosive touring years.
The Rolling Stones Rewind
A visually iconic tribute to the legendary rock band, featuring their famous tongue-and-lips logo on the cover.

A visually iconic tribute to the legendary rock band, featuring their famous tongue-and-lips logo on the cover.

Attributes
  • Model: CUN1

Bound in a striking cover featuring the band's iconic tongue-and-lips logo, this book is a visual celebration of The Rolling Stones' history, style, and stage presence. It likely combines photography and archival material charting the band's evolution from their scrappy beginnings to their status as rock legends.
Adidas Archive
A visual history of Adidas sneakers, showcasing iconic and rare designs from the brand's footwear archive.

This visual archive traces the evolution of Adidas footwear from its origins to its most celebrated modern releases. Packed with detailed photography, the book explores the design innovations, cultural moments, and collaborations that turned Adidas sneakers into enduring style icons, appealing to sneakerheads, designers, and streetwear enthusiasts alike.
André Butzer
A monograph on the German painter known for bold, cartoonish figures in vivid primary colors, blending abstraction with pop sensibility.

This monograph surveys the work of contemporary German painter André Butzer, whose large-scale canvases combine cartoonish, almost childlike figures with a raw painterly intensity. Working primarily in bold primary colors, Butzer's work sits at the crossroads of German Expressionist tradition and pop-inflected abstraction, creating a distinctive, unsettling visual language that has made him one of the notable painters of his generation.
Andy Warhol
An intimate collection of Warhol's early, rarely-seen erotic and romantic line drawings from before his Pop Art fame.

Long before Campbell's soup cans and silkscreened celebrities, Andy Warhol was a working commercial illustrator with a prolific private practice of intimate line drawings. This collection gathers rarely seen sketches from the 1950s depicting male nudes, romantic encounters, and tender same-sex desire — work that reveals a more vulnerable, personal side of Warhol before his rise as the face of American Pop Art.
Anna Atkins
A survey of Atkins' pioneering botanical cyanotype prints, considered among the first photographically illustrated books ever made.

Anna Atkins was a 19th-century botanist and photographer whose cyanotype prints of algae, ferns, and plants are widely regarded as among the earliest photographically illustrated books in history. This collection presents her striking blue-and-white botanical images, celebrating her role as a pioneer at the intersection of science, art, and early photographic technique.
CCCP
Cosmic Communist Constructions Photographed (Frédéric Chaubin) – A striking photo survey of unusual, futuristic Soviet-era architecture built in the final decades of the USSR.

Photographer Frédéric Chaubin spent over a decade traveling through the former Soviet republics documenting extraordinary, often surreal architecture built in the final years of the USSR. The buildings — sanatoriums, research institutes, monuments — showcase a startlingly futuristic and experimental late-Soviet design sensibility rarely associated with Communist-era construction, offering a fascinating counter-narrative to typical Brutalist stereotypes.
Christo and Jeanne Claude
A retrospective on the husband-and-wife artist duo famous for large-scale fabric-wrapped installations and environmental art.

This book chronicles the decades-long collaboration between artists Christo and Jeanne-Claude, famed for their ambitious, temporary large-scale installations — wrapping buildings, bridges, and coastlines in fabric, or installing vast environmental works like floating piers and monumental gates. The book traces their creative process, the logistical challenges of their projects, and their lasting impact on land and public art.
Donald Duck
A comprehensive chronicle of Donald Duck's evolution across animation and comics since his debut.

This comprehensive volume traces the complete history of Donald Duck, from his 1934 debut through decades of animated shorts, comic books, and merchandising. It explores how the hot-tempered, lovable duck became one of the most enduring characters in Disney's stable, with rich visual material spanning classic cartoons, comic panels, and evolving character designs.
Jacques Tati
Filmographie Illustrée / Exploring Tati – A visually driven exploration of French filmmaker Jacques Tati's works, style, and comedic vision.

This visually rich book explores the films, style, and comedic sensibility of French filmmaker Jacques Tati, celebrated for his meticulously choreographed physical comedy and satirical takes on modernity (as seen in Playtime and Mon Oncle). Through illustrated design elements and archival material, it captures Tati's unique blend of visual wit and architectural precision.
Niki De Saint Phalle
An overview of the French-American artist's colorful, playful sculptures and "Nana" figures that challenged traditional gender imagery.

This monograph surveys the life and work of French-American artist Niki de Saint Phalle, best known for her exuberant, brightly colored "Nana" sculptures celebrating the female form, as well as her participation in the Nouveau Réalisme movement and her monumental public art installations. The book traces her transformation from a troubled personal history into one of the boldest voices in 20th-century sculpture.
The Package Design Book
A showcase of award-winning package design from 2008–2026, curated by the Pentawards global design competition.

Curated from the winners of the prestigious Pentawards competition spanning 2008 to 2026, this book showcases the most innovative and eye-catching packaging design from around the world. Covering food, beverage, beauty, and luxury goods packaging, it highlights how creative design can transform ordinary products into memorable branded experiences.
Rothko
An introduction to Mark Rothko's life and iconic color-field paintings, exploring his emotional and spiritual approach to abstraction.

This introductory monograph explores the life and artistic development of Mark Rothko, a leading figure of Abstract Expressionism known for his luminous, layered color-field paintings. The book examines how Rothko sought to evoke profound emotional and spiritual responses through simple compositions of soft-edged rectangular color blocks, and traces his personal struggles alongside his artistic legacy.
Stanley Kubrick
The Stanley Kubrick Archives (Alison Castle, ed.) – An in-depth, estate-authorized look into Kubrick's filmmaking process, drawing on his personal archives and production materials.

Made in cooperation with Kubrick's estate, this extensive volume draws on personal archives, production documents, photographs, and correspondence to offer an unprecedented look into the filmmaker's meticulous creative process. Covering his major works from Dr. Strangelove to Eyes Wide Shut, it provides insight into Kubrick's exacting methods and singular vision as one of cinema's most influential directors.
